description: Measured 2026-09-14 on HEAD 445f71dc6, debug build, fz2 interp, --log-telemetry self time. fixtures2/behavior/cross_kind_operators.fz (102 dbg lines) takes 5.4-5.9s per door; LowerFunction(main) self time 3.1s in one span, AnalyzeActivation(main) rerun 125 times (1.6s). Prefix scaling: 20 lines 4ms/35 reruns, 40 lines 346ms/55, 60 lines 707ms/75, 80 lines 1185ms/95, 102 lines 3088ms/125. Trigger isolated: 100 lines of 'dbg(lt?(a, b))' where lt? is a two-clause guard helper (when a < b) and the 100 calls cycle through K distinct operand-kind pairs: K=1 25ms, K=4 2806ms, K=8 1434ms, K=16 1457ms. Body-position operators (no helper) with 1 pair: 25ms. So each distinct-kind activation of an inlined guard helper makes lowering the CALLER superlinear, and main is re-analyzed once per new callee activation. Consequence: the fixture sits near the CI 20s hang guard (attempt 1 of run 34800809954 tripped it on all three doors alongside the known json_roundtrip/tail_recursion flakes). Note: guard helpers are inlined as nested dispatch plans at every call site today; 8b (guards as pure functions called by the dispatcher) removes that inlining and is the candidate fix; verify with this measurement.
title: Lowering a body that calls a guard helper across distinct operand kinds is superlinear
